content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense (AMD) Sensor, budget line 7265C12000, is a U.S. Army procurement program funded in the Missile Procurement, Army account.", "citation": {"fact_id": "1988a12ef9979f10"}}, {"text": "The Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor (LTAMDS) program provides the required sensing capabilities and surveillance and fire-control quality data for the lower-tier portion of the Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense (AIAMD) of the ballistic-missile-defense battlespace.", "citation": {"fact_id": "515b0fcf4b27f2c4"}}, {"text": "The LTAMDS radar increases sensor performance to maximize the inherent capabilities of the PATRIOT Advanced Capability (PAC-3) Missile Segment Enhanced (MSE) interceptor to engage threats.", "citation": {"fact_id": "515b0fcf4b27f2c4"}}, {"text": "The funding line is directly aligned to the Army Air and Missile Defense Modernization priority and supports the Air and Missile Defense Cross Functional Team (AMD CFT).", "citation": {"fact_id": "71da182b1165220a"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total FY2026 request is $1,255,473 thousand (about $1.26 billion), a sharp rise from the $387,629 thousand enacted in FY2025.", "citation": {"fact_id": "68875d7b74223d18"}}, {"text": "In FY2024 the program recorded actual spending of $149,599 thousand (about $150 million), so the FY2026 request is more than eight times its FY2024 execution level.", "citation": {"fact_id": "1988a12ef9979f10"}}, {"text": "The FY2026 request splits into $637,473 thousand of discretionary procurement and $618,000 thousand of reconciliation (mandatory) funding.", "citation": {"fact_id": "577f10f12c011321"}}, {"text": "The program narrative confirms the FY2026 request totals $1,255,473 thousand, with the $618,000 thousand of mandatory funds procuring 4 Low-Rate Initial Production sensors and ancillary equipment in FY2026, and further detail provided in Section 20003 (Missile Defense) of the Reconciliation Exhibit.", "citation": {"fact_id": "71da182b1165220a"}}, {"text": "The narrative attributes a $249.844 million increase in FY2026 base discretionary procurement dollars over FY2025 to increased production and initial-fielding walk-up activities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "71da182b1165220a"}}, {"text": "The reconciliation portion is captured in the mandatory FY2026 request line of $618,000 thousand in Missile Procurement, Army.", "citation": {"fact_id": "791326ff87682c37"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Army, with funding drawn from the Missile Procurement, Army appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "68875d7b74223d18"}}, {"text": "The effort supports the Air and Missile Defense Cross Functional Team (AMD CFT) and is aligned to the Army Air and Missile Defense Modernization priority.", "citation": {"fact_id": "71da182b1165220a"}}, {"text": "The sensor is designed to work with the PATRIOT Advanced Capability (PAC-3) Missile Segment Enhanced (MSE) interceptor within the Army Integrated Air and Missile Defense architecture.", "citation": {"fact_id":
